question: How do I diagnose intermittent packet loss on an LTE bearer?
answer: Capture at multiple points: UE-side tcpdump, eNB S1-U mirror, PGW SGi mirror. Correlate timestamps. If loss appears at S1-U but not SGi, the issue is transport between eNB and SGW. If present at UE but not eNB, it's a radio issue - examine HARQ retransmission rates.

question: What causes RSRQ degradation in dense urban deployments?
answer: RSRQ = N * RSRP / RSSI. In dense urban, RSSI rises from interfering cells, pulling RSRQ down even with good RSRP. Mitigations: eICIC with almost-blank subframes, PCI planning to avoid same-frequency collisions, antenna down-tilt to reduce overshoot, FeICIC with CRE for HetNet.

question: Why would a UE reattach repeatedly every few minutes?
answer: Common causes: (1) T3412 timer misconfigured - periodic TAU timer too short. (2) UE losing coverage and re-entering (check RSRP variability). (3) Battery optimization on device forcing PDN deactivate. (4) Paging DRX misalignment causing UE to miss paging and MME to detach. (5) MME-side implicit detach timer hitting.

question: How to troubleshoot one-way audio in VoLTE calls?
answer: One-way audio = RTP flowing in one direction only. Check: (1) NAT on signaling vs media paths. (2) SBC media anchoring - SDP c= line pointing to unreachable IP. (3) Firewall blocking RTP on one side. (4) MGW codec mismatch - re-INVITE for codec change failed. (5) Capture RTP streams at SBC to confirm flow direction.

question: What does a high RRC connection re-establishment rate indicate?
answer: High RRC re-est rate = UEs losing RRC connection (radio link failure) and trying to resume. Indicates: (1) Coverage holes - UEs moving out of range. (2) Interference bursts. (3) Too-aggressive handover parameters causing HOF. (4) eNB software issue dropping contexts. Target <1% of total connections; >3% needs investigation.

question: How do I identify PIM (passive intermodulation) at a cell site?
answer: PIM signature: uplink interference showing as elevated noise floor at specific frequencies = f(downlink carriers). Steps: (1) Use sweep/PIM tester on site. (2) Check connectors, weatherproofing, loose hardware. (3) Look for rusted metal objects near antennas (guy wires, bolts). (4) Verify jumper cable quality. PIM typically worsens with power/load.

question: Why is 5G NSA dual connectivity not activating for a UE?
answer: NSA requires LTE anchor + NR secondary cell. Checks: (1) UE 5G capability reported in Attach (UE-NR-Capability IE). (2) LTE anchor cell has X2 to gNB. (3) B1 measurement event configured for NR. (4) SgNB Addition Request succeeds over Xn/X2. (5) UE in coverage of both LTE and NR simultaneously.

question: Troubleshoot BGP flapping on core router
answer: Flapping = repeated up/down of BGP session. Check: (1) TCP 179 reachability - MTU issues cause TCP session resets. (2) Hold timer vs keepalive mismatch. (3) MD5 auth key mismatch. (4) Route damping triggering. (5) CPU spikes on peer. (6) Underlying link flapping (check interface counters). Logs on both ends + timing correlation key.

question: What is the procedure for investigating MME overload?
answer: Symptoms: high S1-AP processing delay, attach rejections with cause 22 (congestion). Steps: (1) CPU and memory on MME nodes. (2) S1-AP message rate - compare to capacity. (3) Pool balancing - is one MME hotter than others? (4) Diameter S6a response time from HSS. (5) Enable MME overload protection (reject low-priority traffic). (6) Long-term: scale horizontally.

question: How to isolate Wi-Fi offload issues when ANDSF is configured
answer: User device not offloading to Wi-Fi despite policy. Check: (1) ANDSF rules pushed to UE (via OMA-DM). (2) UE OS honors 3GPP Wi-Fi offload (varies by vendor). (3) SSID match and credentials. (4) ePDG reachable for S2b IPSec tunnel (trusted/untrusted WLAN). (5) AAA interaction on SWm for authorization. Capture on ePDG will show IKE exchange.

question: Diagnose SCTP association failures between eNB and MME
answer: SCTP underpins S1-AP. Failures: (1) INIT chunk blocked by firewall (SCTP protocol 132). (2) Asymmetric routing breaking multi-homed paths. (3) Heartbeat interval mismatch. (4) Path MTU discovery issues with DF bit. (5) sctpdump on MME to see INIT/INIT-ACK. Most networks use single-homed SCTP to avoid multi-homing complexity.

question: Why are CSFB calls failing to establish on target 3G cell?
answer: CSFB redirects to UTRAN. Failures: (1) SRVCC not actually needed here - this is CSFB, check SGs path. (2) No UTRAN coverage at UE location. (3) Gs interface between SGSN and MSC down. (4) Location Update to MSC fails (IMSI not in VLR). (5) MSC paging timer expires before UE completes RAU. Logs on MSC show final cause.

question: How to troubleshoot DNS for IMS P-CSCF discovery?
answer: Three discovery methods: (1) DHCP option 120 (most common). (2) PCO in Attach (3GPP native). (3) Pre-configured on UE. If failing: verify PCO returned by PGW contains P-CSCF IPv4/v6. If using DHCP, trace DHCP discover/offer. Test: UE performs DNS SRV query for _sip._udp.<domain> - should return P-CSCF address.

question: What causes high call setup time (PDD) in VoLTE?
answer: Post-dial delay >3s is noticeable. Contributors: (1) DNS lookup for called number ENUM. (2) SIP INVITE routing hops (P-CSCF -> S-CSCF -> AS chain). (3) HSS Sh interface slow for user profile. (4) Dedicated bearer activation adds ~200ms for QCI 1. (5) Precondition negotiation per 3GPP profile. Measure each hop with correlated logs.

question: Investigating elevated UE power consumption on a specific network
answer: UE drains battery faster than expected. Possible: (1) DRX not configured well - UE not sleeping. (2) Poor coverage forces max TX power. (3) Constant network reselection due to low RSRP. (4) Application keeping radio active (chatty heartbeats). (5) No RRC Release after idle - eNB keeping UE connected. Review DRX params and eNB inactivity timers.

question: Why would throughput cap at exactly 100 Mbps?
answer: Exact cap = configuration limit, not physical. Check: (1) AMBR on subscriber profile (APN-AMBR or UE-AMBR). (2) Transport interface speed (1GbE half-duplex = ~100). (3) PGW policy engine rate limit. (4) OCS quota applying throttling post-quota. (5) Test with different SIM/subscription to isolate.

question: How to troubleshoot roaming SMS failures
answer: SMS via MAP (legacy) or Diameter (newer). Check: (1) HPLMN SMSC routing rules for VPLMN. (2) Global Title Translation on STP. (3) SCCP routing between HPLMN/VPLMN. (4) SRI-SM (Send Routing Info for SMS) succeeding. (5) For Diameter-based: SY/SLh interfaces. Capture on STP / Diameter edge.

question: What is causing high number of Service Request failures?
answer: Service Request by UE transitioning IDLE->CONNECTED. Failures: (1) Authentication failed (SIM sync issue). (2) Security mode command failed. (3) NAS count mismatch - common after abnormal release. (4) Bearer establishment fails (see ESM cause). Aggregate by EMM cause on MME to find pattern.

question: How to debug silent call (no audio after answer) in VoLTE
answer: Signaling OK, 200 OK received, but no media. Check: (1) SDP offer/answer IP/port - are both sides sending to correct destination? (2) SRTP key mismatch - if encrypted media fails, it drops silently. (3) Dedicated QCI 1 bearer not established - voice uses default bearer with no QoS. (4) NAT pinhole closed before media start.

question: Why would a specific device model fail to attach while others succeed?
answer: Device-specific attach failure. Investigate: (1) UE-Radio-Capability IE - unusual band combination? (2) UE modem firmware - known bugs? (3) SIM applet version - STK interactions. (4) Specific PLMN/frequency combination. Reproduce with same SIM in different device vs same device with different SIM to isolate.

question: How do I troubleshoot degraded HARQ performance on uplink?
answer: HARQ BLER target typically 10% first transmission, <1% after 4 retransmissions. If poor: (1) UE TX power limited (check PHR reports). (2) Uplink SINR low due to interference. (3) PUSCH allocation too aggressive (high MCS for the SINR). (4) Timing advance error. Link budget analysis with scheduler logs finds the culprit.

question: What does a failing X2 setup between two eNBs typically indicate?
answer: X2 carries handover and interference coordination. Setup failures: (1) IP transport unreachable (ping test). (2) SCTP port 36422 blocked. (3) PLMN ID mismatch between eNBs. (4) TAC list doesn't align. (5) MME configuration has both eNBs? Check X2SetupFailure cause IE on the initiating eNB.

question: Troubleshoot APN-AMBR not being applied correctly
answer: APN-AMBR caps aggregate non-GBR traffic on APN. Check: (1) Subscribed value in HSS. (2) Value delivered in Create Session Response to MME. (3) Value enforced on PGW and SGW (ingress + egress). (4) Policy dynamic update via PCRF Gx - CCA-Update may override. Trace Gx for real-time overrides.

question: How to investigate HSS overload during mass re-registration events
answer: Re-reg storms (e.g. after outage recovery) overload HSS. Mitigations: (1) HSS overload protection - reject low-priority AIRs. (2) Randomize T3412 to stagger UEs. (3) MME implicit detach with staggered timers. (4) Rate limit on Diameter DRA. (5) Scale HSS capacity. Monitor S6a response times.

question: Why is lawful intercept not capturing certain users?
answer: LI misses require careful investigation (and formal procedures). Technical causes: (1) X1 provisioning on wrong network element. (2) User's traffic routed via different PGW than targeted. (3) Encrypted bearer content (LI may only get metadata). (4) SGi-LAN tap missing the flow. This requires coordination with LEA and should follow legal process.

question: Elevated CPU on SBC during peak hours
answer: SBC CPU scaling. Check: (1) Transcoding load - are unnecessary codec conversions happening? (2) TLS/SRTP termination cost. (3) DoS filter triggering on legitimate traffic. (4) SIP message rate - chatty endpoints? (5) DNS lookup per call (cache misses). Mitigate: enable SRTP pass-through where possible, add transcoding DSP resources.

question: How do I identify the source of unexpected IPv6 neighbor discovery traffic
answer: NS/NA flooding observed. Steps: (1) Packet capture on affected segment. (2) Identify MAC addresses of originators. (3) Check for misconfigured router advertisements (multiple routers). (4) MLD snooping disabled causing multicast flood. (5) Malfunctioning device periodically re-discovering. Fix at source.

question: What causes intermittent TCP resets on SGi egress?
answer: TCP RSTs from operator side to internet. Causes: (1) Session table overflow on CGNAT - flow evicted. (2) Firewall TCP idle timeout shorter than app keepalive. (3) Load balancer re-hashing. (4) MTU/MSS issues causing fragmentation drop then RST. (5) DPI injecting RST for policy violation. Capture on SGi will show RST origin.

question: Troubleshoot GTP-U tunnel drops between eNB and SGW
answer: GTP-U over UDP 2152. Drops: (1) MTU issues - if packets fragmented and reassembly fails. (2) UDP checksum errors. (3) TEID mismatch - session state divergence. (4) Firewall stateful inspection breaking flow. (5) ECMP hash flapping causing out-of-order. Capture GTP with tshark, check sequence numbers per TEID.

question: Why is a specific APN giving slow DNS responses only?
answer: Slow DNS on one APN = per-APN config issue. Check: (1) DNS server in PCO for this APN - is it reachable from PGW egress? (2) DNS server load (separate per-APN servers sometimes). (3) ACL delay on APN firewall. (4) Recursive lookup path longer for this DNS. (5) UDP 53 vs TCP 53 fallback working? Test with dig from PGW SGi interface.
